text:
alex.carter: Heads up — noticed repeated 403s from the kms-proxy to an unfamiliar IP (44.55.66.77) and a burst of token refresh attempts. Looks like someone had a credential and is hitting the proxy but failing RBAC checks.
maria.gomez: Can you paste the raw lines?
alex.carter: ```
2026-03-19T12:02:03Z WARN kms-proxy request from=44.55.66.77 svc=svc-webhook action=unwrap token_id=tok-xxxxx status=403
2026-03-19T12:02:07Z WARN kms-proxy request from=44.55.66.77 svc=svc-webhook action=unwrap token_id=tok-yyyyy status=403
```
jonathan.h: If it's token_id churn + wrong role, could be an old webhook key leaked. Who owns svc-webhook?
sam.ibrahim: svc-webhook is owned by integrations team (team-infra). It uses a short-lived client cert + proxy API key.
devops-oncall: @sam.ibrahim — can you revoke that proxy API key immediately and patch ingress to block 44.55.66.77?
sam.ibrahim: Doing revoke now. Command: `vault write auth/token/revoke token=tok-xxxxx` then rotate the proxy key in k8s secret `kms-proxy-secret`.
security-bot: Alert: token tok-xxxxx revoked by sam.ibrahim at 2026-03-19T12:05:10Z. AuditID=au-9987.
maria.gomez: Also reducing RBAC for svc-webhook to only unwrap with specific key IDs — will apply a scoped policy in Vault and push. Quick patch: `vault policy write svc-webhook-policy - <<EOF
path "transit/decrypt/webhook-key" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
EOF`
jonathan.h: Good. We should also rotate any service account keys that could be used to mint tokens against the proxy. Run `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-webhook@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and revoke old ones.
alex.carter: I'll run a scan for other IPs and known indicators. Running quick grep across proxy logs for last 72h.
security-bot: Scheduled audit-export: /exports/kms-proxy/2026-03-19-1200.tar.gz (contains request meta, truncated payloads).
devops-oncall: For containment: 1) revoke proxy API key 2) patch kube secret with new key 3) block 44.55.66.77 in firewall 4) reduce svc-webhook RBAC 5) rotate SA keys 6) enable full audit_log retention for 30d. Who's taking 1-3?
sam.ibrahim: Taking 1 & 2 now (rolling deploy). ETA 15m.
maria.gomez: Taking 4 & 6. Will add policy and bump audit to 30d.
jonathan.h: I'll handle 5 (SA key rotation) and notify cloud infra.
alex.carter: Quick note for legal/notifications — we need to know if any customer data was involved. Early signs show only token unwrap attempts (403) so unlikely data exfil; but keep in memory. @legal-ops please standby.
legal-ops: Acknowledge. Please collect timestamps and affected principals; we'll advise on disclosure if needed.
security-bot: Post-incident checklist created: actions assigned (sam.ibrahim, maria.gomez, jonathan.h). Next steps: run credential blast-radius script and search repos for hardcoded proxy key.
alex.carter: Found 1 suspicious reference in a partner repo mirror — pinging partner Slack DM. `repo:partner/integrations` file `deploy/prod.env` contains `KMS_PROXY_KEY=redacted`.
sam.ibrahim: Oof. We'll ask partner to rotate their copy and confirm deletion. Add to remediation: remote repo search + partner coord.
maria.gomez: After rotation, schedule a canary rollout for kms-proxy with stricter rate limits and JWT-only auth for unwrap endpoints.
jonathan.h: Also propose enabling conditional policies that require request origin tag (k8s namespace) and short TTLs.
alex.carter: Timeline: containment done in ~25m, rotation complete in ~40m. Follow-up: incident doc and post-incident review tomorrow 10:00. Anyone object?
legal-ops: No objections. We'll prep communications if partner confirms leak.
security-bot: Reminder: create Jira SECURITY-xxxxx with all actions and assign to eng-security.
sam.ibrahim: Created SEC-2026, linking audit export.
maria.gomez: Afterwrap: add a periodic scan for `KMS_PROXY_KEY|kms-proxy-secret` strings in public forks and add partner onboarding checklist to prevent storing keys in repo.
alex.carter: Thanks all — keep updates here. If anyone sees new IPs or successful unwraps, escalate to pager. :thumbsup:
